gap: No result ChatGPT got states that buying a NAS just for this costs more than hosting for years: the cheapest Docker-capable UGREEN, the DXP2800, is $389.99 before drives (UGREEN store, 2026-11-17), while Hostinger Premium is $95.52 for 48 months, so the NAS only pulls ahead in year 7 even before drives. They also don't state that UGREEN's own FAQ says the cheapest UGREEN, the $239.99 DH2300, does not officially support Docker.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and cited no pages, so there are no rival pages to compare against. Its own answer's cost table says it 'assumes you already own the NAS' and 'excludes hardware depreciation'. It names Synology DS923+/DS224+ without prices, recommends Docker without saying which NAS models can't run it, and gives no break-even. Our current page has the DXP2800 price and host prices but no break-even arithmetic and no DH2300 warning.
decides: For a shopper who doesn't own a NAS, 'instead of paying for hosting' turns from yes into no: Hostinger Premium ($1.99/mo prepaid 48 months, then $10.99/mo) stays cheaper than a DXP2800 plus power until year 7, and a $4/mo DigitalOcean Droplet stays cheaper for about 10.6 years, drives excluded. For a shopper who does own one, ChatGPT's 'yes' stands, but only on a Docker-capable model, so the DH2300 must be called out as unsuitable. If the shopper buys anyway, the pick is the DXP2800 ($389.99) or the DH4300 Plus ($373.99), not the DH2300 ($239.99).
